1  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER DICTATION, THIS  DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:20122  WP No. 22301 of 2021  ORDER Respondent No. 1 filed a claim petition stating that she was traveling in an autorickshaw, seated in the dickey with her legs extending out of the vehicle and facing the traffic behind.
The autorickshaw was struck from the rear by a tractor, which was being driven by the petitioner in a rash and negligent manner, causing injuries to Respondent No. 1's legs.

2. The petitioner was named as a respondent in the claim petition and subsequently filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure to implead the driver of the autorickshaw.

The charge sheet filed by the police attributed composite negligence to both the petitioner and the autorickshaw driver, citing offences under Sections 187, 177, 196, and 146 of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Sections 227 and 337 of the Indian Penal Code.
However, the Tribunal rejected the application, stating that Respondent No.1 sought compensation solely from the petitioner.
3. The Tribunal framed an issue regarding whether the respondent could prove composite negligence as asserted in the claim petition.
4. The police investigation concluded with a charge sheet against both the petitioner, who was driving the tractor, and the driver of the autorickshaw, indicating contributory negligence.
The petitioner contends that the autorickshaw driver pleaded guilty before the jurisdictional Magistrate.
Therefore, when composite NC: 2024:KHC:20122 negligence is attributed, the autorickshaw driver becomes a necessary party to the claim petition.

This is crucial for determining the extent of negligence between the joint tort feasors, which would allow one party to recover the sum from the other after making full payment to the plaintiff/claimant, as mandated by the liability satisfied by the other.

5. The Honorable Supreme Court, in the case of *Khenyei vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.*,
[2015] 5 SCR 158, held:
"(iii) In cases where all joint tortfeasors have been impleaded and the evidence is sufficient, it is open to the court/tribunal to determine the inter se extent of composite negligence of the drivers.

If both parties have been impleaded and the apportionment/extent of their Sri Shivakumar vs Smt Shanthamma on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80941504/
2 negligence has been determined by the court/tribunal, one joint tortfeasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings."

6. Therefore, when the petitioner/respondent in the claim petition has specifically attributed composite negligence to the driver of the autorickshaw, and the charge sheet has corroborated this,
the autorickshaw driver is a necessary party to the claim petition to establish composite negligence.

Failure to implead the driver would deprive the petitioner of the right to recover the amount from the driver after making whole payment to the claimant to the extent of the driver's liability in case of composite negligee is established.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:20122 ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned order dated 22.4.2021 passed on IA filed in MVC No.287/2019 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Pandavapura vide Annexure-A is hereby quashed, and the application is allowed.
iii) The claimant therein to implead the proposed respondent in the application filed by the petitioner on providing , and after providing an opportunity to all the parties to proceed further in the matter in accordance with law.
iv) All contentions relating to the liability as also the quantum are left open.
